propositions: A gate run does not warn when the running build's commit is a strict ancestor of the pinned base ref sha, allowing stale code to silently process current config and code changes.

When a gate resolves the base ref to a pinned sha, it should emit an advisory warning (exactly once per build-sha/pinned-sha pair) naming the build commit, its date, pinned sha, and drift count in commits, without failing the run or altering the verdict.
Unknown config keys should be reported with different wording when drift is detected (indicating the build may predate the key) versus when no drift is detected (typo wording).
Build commit resolution must gracefully handle unavailable provenance, commits absent from the target repo, and cases where the gate code and target repo are different repositories.
